result:
The proposed answer of 1/2 is most likely wrong. The true value is probably 1/3, based on my recollection of the literature on feedback vertex sets in bounded-degree oriented graphs. I have not verified that from a source here.

The proof also has gaps regardless of the final value:

- **Upper bound:** The max-cut argument correctly gives induced maximum degree at most 2 on each side. But components can be odd cycles, which have independent sets smaller than half their size, so the claimed bound $|I| \ge n/2$ does not follow.
- **Lower bound:** The claim that every acyclic set in the Eulerian 4-regular expander has size at most $n/2 + o(n)$ is asserted without proof. An acyclic set is not the same as an independent set, so bounding independent sets does not bound acyclic sets. Nothing shown establishes this bound.

If the true answer were 1/2, it would contradict the $n/3$ bound I recall, so the lower-bound construction is the step most likely to fail.

VERDICT: REJECT
CONFIDENCE: 4
